newsitem.title: BELGIUM: European car group rejects Commission sales claim.
newsitem.headline: European car group rejects Commission sales claim.

text.p: A leading European car manufacturers' group on Friday dismissed as excessive European Commission forecasts of 5.4 percent growth in 1996 car sales.

James Rosenstein, spokesman for the European Automobile Manufacturers Association (ACEA), said the commission's forecast of sales of 13,545,000 units for this year did not take market reality into account.

The Commission -- the EU's executive -- included a revised forecast on vehicle sales while announcing on Friday that it would increase Japan's export allowance by a further 13,000 cars to 1,079,000 for 1996.
Rosenstein said ACEA figures suggested that growth of European vehicle sales this year would be limited to 4.5 percent.
"There has been 6.6 percent growth through September, but this has been driven by good sales in France. The market reality is that elsewhere in the EU, sales are flat or down," he said.
French sales soared in September as buyers took advantage of a state incentive scheme.
Rosenstein dismissed the export increase granted to Japan as "largely symbolic", but questioned the need to increase what is anyway an under-utilised quota.
Japan and the EU have an informal agreement to monitor vehicle trade until the end of the century with direct Japanese exports being based on a percentage of actual sales in the 15-member bloc.
The ACEA said Japan had exported some 598,000 vehicles to Europe up to the end of August.

A Commission spokesman said forecasting vehicle sales "was not an exact science", but stressed that the increase given to Japan, although unlikely to be used, was neccessary to reflect accurate monitoring of the EU/Japan agreement.
The deal started in 1990 following objections from Britain, France, Italy, Portugal and Spain over imports of Japanese vehicles.
